escalations.title: handlebars — Server-Side Template Injection / Remote Code Execution
escalations.description: GHSA-2w6w-674q-4c4q. Crafted template strings can execute arbitrary JavaScript on the server. An attacker who can influence template input can achieve full RCE.
escalations.exploit_scenario: User-controlled input reaches a handlebars.compile() call. Attacker injects JS prototype pollution or function execution payload. Server executes attacker code.
escalations.remediation: Update handlebars to >=4.7.9 in Source/Backend. Audit all template compile calls for user-controlled input. Consider migrating to a safer templating library (mustache, nunjucks).

escalations.title: vitest — Arbitrary File Read / Code Execution via UI Server
escalations.description: GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp. When vitest --ui is running, any user reachable to the UI server port can read arbitrary filesystem files or execute code.
escalations.exploit_scenario: CI runner or shared dev machine exposes vitest --ui on a network interface. Attacker requests arbitrary file paths through the UI server API, retrieving .env files, SSH keys, source code.
escalations.remediation: Update vitest to >=4.1.10 in Source/Frontend and portal/Frontend. Audit CI jobs for vitest --ui usage. Ensure UI server never binds to non-loopback interfaces.

escalations.cvss: Critical (CVSS not published at audit time)
escalations.title: protobufjs — Arbitrary Code Execution in Message Parsing
escalations.description: Crafted protobuf messages can trigger code execution during deserialization in protobufjs. Any service deserializing gRPC messages from untrusted sources is vulnerable.
escalations.exploit_scenario: Attacker sends a crafted gRPC message to portal/Backend. The protobufjs parser executes attacker-controlled code during message deserialization, achieving RCE on the portal backend.
escalations.remediation: Run: cd portal/Backend && npm audit | grep protobufjs to confirm transitive path and available patches. Apply patch immediately upon availability. As interim: validate all gRPC message origins; consider wrapping deserialization in try/catch with strict schema validation.

escalations.title: form-data — HTTP Header Injection via CRLF in Multipart Boundaries
escalations.description: CRLF characters in multipart form field names can inject arbitrary HTTP headers, enabling response splitting, cache poisoning, or session fixation attacks.
escalations.exploit_scenario: Attacker submits a multipart form field with a name containing CRLF sequences. The form-data library includes these characters in the Content-Disposition header, injecting arbitrary headers into the response.
escalations.remediation: Update form-data to a patched version. Run npm audit fix in affected projects.

escalations.title: postcss — Cross-Site Scripting via Unescaped </style> Tags in CSS Output
escalations.description: postcss fails to escape </style> tags in generated CSS, allowing XSS if user-controlled CSS content is rendered in a browser <style> block.
escalations.exploit_scenario: Application renders user-controlled CSS in a <style> block. Attacker injects </style><script>alert(1)</script> into a CSS value. postcss does not escape this; the browser closes the <style> block and executes the script.
escalations.remediation: Update postcss to a patched version. Ensure user-controlled content is never rendered in <style> blocks without sanitisation.

escalations.title: nanoid — Non-Cryptographically-Secure ID Generation — Verify Not Used for Security Tokens
escalations.description: nanoid uses a non-CSPRNG source in some configurations, making generated IDs predictable. If nanoid is used to generate session tokens, CSRF tokens, or password reset tokens, those can be guessed.
escalations.exploit_scenario: Application uses nanoid to generate a password reset token or CSRF token. Due to weak randomness, an attacker can enumerate or predict valid token values, bypassing the security control.
escalations.remediation: Audit all nanoid usage. If used for security-sensitive tokens, replace with crypto.randomUUID() or crypto.randomBytes(). Update nanoid package if a patched version is available.

TheFixer.title: @grpc/grpc-js — Server Crash via Malformed gRPC Requests
TheFixer.description: GHSA-5375-pq7m-f5r2. Malformed gRPC requests crash the portal/Backend server. Repeated requests cause sustained availability loss.

TheFixer.title: GET /api/search endpoint not wired — DependencyPicker typeahead broken
TheFixer.description: FR-dependency-search requires GET /api/search?q= for cross-entity typeahead. Route handler does not exist in Source/Backend/src/app.ts. DependencyPicker.tsx calls this endpoint; every query returns 404.
TheFixer.remediation: Create Source/Backend/src/routes/search.ts with a handler filtering the in-memory store by title/description. Register in app.ts as app.use('/api', searchRouter). Add // Verifies: FR-dependency-search. Sanitise the ?q= query parameter.
TheFixer.security_note: Input sanitisation required when implementing — flagged for TheGuardians review (ESC-001 cross-ref: injection risk if user input flows into template engine).

TheFixer.title: Traceability enforcer scans only 12% of total requirements
TheFixer.description: tools/traceability-enforcer.py:70 hard-codes source_dirs=['Source','E2E']. 95 of 108 requirements in portal/ and platform/ are excluded. CI gate reports TRACEABILITY PASSED while these directories are never verified.
TheFixer.remediation: Extend source_dirs to ['Source', 'E2E', 'portal', 'platform']. Add a second scan pass targeting Specifications/ requirement IDs. Update spec-drift-report.json generator to scan the same extended dirs.

TheFixer.title: 3 silent catch blocks swallow errors — CLAUDE.md violation
TheFixer.description: portal/Frontend/src/components/common/RepoSelector.tsx:20, BugDetail.tsx:82, and FeatureRequestDetail.tsx:80 all use .catch(() => {}) with no log, re-throw, or documentation.
TheFixer.remediation: Add // repo list is non-critical UI enhancement — fail silently comment on each .catch(() => {}) block, or preferably log: .catch((err) => logger.warn('repo list failed', { err })).

TheFixer.title: FR-TMP-001 missing source tag; FR-TMP-008 has wrong tag
TheFixer.description: platform/orchestrator/lib/workflow-engine.js implements FR-TMP-001 (risk classification) at ~line 1096 but has no // Verifies: FR-TMP-001 comment. platform/Dockerfile.worker:3 has // Verifies: dev-crew unified repo — Task 3 Step 2 instead of // Verifies: FR-TMP-008.
TheFixer.remediation: Add // Verifies: FR-TMP-001 — extract riskLevel from leader output at ~line 1096 in workflow-engine.js. Update Dockerfile.worker:3 to // Verifies: FR-TMP-008 — gh CLI and Playwright installed.

TheFixer.title: 113 console.log calls in platform orchestrator — production code should use structured logger
TheFixer.description: platform/orchestrator/lib/workflow-engine.js contains 113 raw console.log calls. CLAUDE.md mandates structured JSON logging; console.log bypasses OTel trace correlation and Prometheus metrics.
TheFixer.remediation: Replace console.log calls with the project logger (logger.info, logger.debug, etc.) to ensure trace IDs propagate and log output is structured JSON in production.

TheFixer.title: eslint-disable-next-line suppressing hook dependency warnings without explanation
TheFixer.description: Source/Frontend/src/hooks/useWorkItems.ts:63 and DependencyPicker.tsx:82 suppress react-hooks/exhaustive-deps with no inline comment explaining the intentional omission.
TheFixer.remediation: Add inline comment explaining why the dependency is excluded (e.g. // intentionally omit X — would cause infinite loop), or restructure the effect to avoid suppression.

TheFixer.title: Hardcoded http://localhost:${port} URL in CycleCard component
TheFixer.description: portal/Frontend/src/components/orchestrator/CycleCard.tsx:112 hardcodes the scheme and host. In any non-localhost deployment (staging, CI preview, Docker network), this link will be wrong.
TheFixer.remediation: Derive the URL from a shared config/env var (e.g. VITE_APP_BASE_URL or a getAppUrl(port) helper).
